title: Lifting of sections of etale algebras implies henselian pair
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that for every ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every $A$-algebra map $\sigma:A'\to A/I$ there is an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A'\to A$ whose composite with $A\to A/I$ is $\sigma$. Then $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and the pair $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), implications (2)$\Rightarrow$(4)$\Rightarrow$(3) and their proof (first paragraph: $I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}A$ via $A\to A_f$; $IB$ in the radical of an integral $B$ by going up, Algebra Lemmas Tag 00GU (lemma-integral-going-up) and Tag 00HZ (lemma-going-up-closed); injectivity by Lemma Tag 09XF (lemma-idempotents-determined-modulo-radical); existence by Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs)); (4)$\Rightarrow$(3) trivial since finite algebras are integral

proof.text: *$I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}A$.* Suppose not: there is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ with $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $I+\mathfrak m=A$ ($\mathfrak m$ maximal) and $1=i+f$ with $i\in I$, $f\in\mathfrak m$; $f\equiv1$ modulo $I$ and $f$ is not a unit. Let $A'=A_f$ (localization at the powers of $f$). $\operatorname{Spec}A_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1). The image of $f$ in $A/I$ is $1$, a unit, so by the universal property of localization the quotient map $A\to A/I$ extends to an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:A_f\to A/I$. By hypothesis there is an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A_f\to A$; then $f=\tau(f/1)$ and $1=\tau((f/1)(1/f))=f\cdot\tau(1/f)$, so $f$ is a unit of $A$, a contradiction. Hence $I$ lies in every maximal ideal, i.e. in the Jacobson radical of $A$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (2)$\Rightarrow$(4): 'Then $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, since otherwise there would be a nonunit $f\in A$ congruent to $1$ modulo $I$ and the map $A\to A_f$ would contradict (2)'; the existence of $f$ and the unit computation written out by the agent

proof.text: *$IB$ lies in the radical of a finite $B$.* Let $B$ be a finite $A$-algebra. $B$ is integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Since $I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}A$ (step 1), $IB$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical] (every maximal ideal of $B$ lies over a maximal ideal of $A$, which contains $I$).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI, (2)$\Rightarrow$(4): 'Hence $IB\subset B$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $B$ for $B$ integral over $A$ because $\Spec(B)\to\Spec(A)$ is closed by Algebra, Lemmas 00HZ and 00GU'; and '(4)$\Rightarrow$(3) is trivial' (finite algebras are integral)

proof.text: *Uniqueness of lifts.* Let $B$ be a finite $A$-algebra and $e_1,e_2\in B$ idempotents with the same image in $B/IB$. Then $e_1-e_2\in IB$, which lies in the Jacobson radical of $B$ (step 2), so $e_1=e_2$ [lem-weil-pbc-idempotents-determined-modulo-radical] (with $R=B$, $J=IB$).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI, (2)$\Rightarrow$(4): 'Thus the map from idempotents of $B$ to idempotents of $B/IB$ is injective by Lemma 09XF'

proof.text: *Existence of lifts.* Let $B$ be a finite $A$-algebra and $\bar e\in B/IB$ an idempotent. $B$ is integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs] there are a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale, such that $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_AA'$ mapped to $\bar e$ by $\rho:B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B\otimes_A(A/I)=B/IB$. Let $\sigma:A'\to A'/IA'\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}A/I$; it is an $A$-algebra map ($\alpha$ is induced by the structure map, so $\alpha^{-1}$ is $A$-linear). By hypothesis there is an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A'\to A$ with $q\circ\tau=\sigma$, $q:A\to A/I$ the quotient map. Let $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\tau:B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_AA=B$, a ring map, and $e=\varphi(e')$, an idempotent of $B$ (ring maps preserve idempotents). Its image in $B/IB=B\otimes_A(A/I)$ is $(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes q)(\varphi(e'))=(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes(q\circ\tau))(e')=(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\sigma)(e')=\rho(e')=\bar e$, since $\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\sigma$ and $\rho$ are the same map (both are $b\otimes a'\mapsto b\otimes\alpha^{-1}(a'\bmod IA')$). So $e$ lifts $\bar e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI, (2)$\Rightarrow$(4): 'On the other hand, since (2) holds, every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts to an idempotent of $B$ by Lemma 07M4'; the descent of the idempotent from $B\otimes_AA'$ to $B$ along the section supplied by (2) is left implicit in Stacks and written out by the agent

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 3 and 4, for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$, i.e. $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]; and $I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}A$ by step 1. (Stacks proves the lifting for all integral $B$, its condition (4), and specializes to finite $B$, condition (3); steps 2-4 run the same argument directly for finite $B$.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI: 'In this way we see that (2) implies (4). The implication (4)$\Rightarrow$(3) is trivial.'

lean.statement: theorem henselianRing_of_etale_section_lifting (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (h : ∀ (A' : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A'] [Algebra.Etale A A'] (σ : A' →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I), ∃ τ : A' →ₐ[A] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A I).comp τ = σ) : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥ ∧ HenselianRing A I ∧ ∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] (e₀ : B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)), IsIdempotentElem e₀ → ∃! e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) e = e₀
